messages:
Maya: quick overnight handoff — high level first. We had a regional egress failure (us-west) affecting model-serving responses between 02:10–02:45 UTC. Symptoms: increased 502 from egress-proxy, automatic fallback to smaller model variant triggered, some requests hit request-timeout retries (client saw ~1.2s tail latency increase). Customer impact: small percentage (~3%) of steady traffic saw degraded quality due to fallback; a handful of low-volume customers reported partial failures during spikes. No data loss.

Maya: timeline in short:
- 02:09 ops-bot page: egress-proxy 502 surge
- 02:12 auto-routing kicked: traffic rerouted to fallback region (us-east) and to model-variant v1-small
- 02:20 deploy-bot executed temporary circuit-breaker rule for noisy IP range (rate-limit)
- 02:45 root-cause narrowed: transient NAT gateway exhaustion in us-west cloud region; provider throttled new connections.
- 02:50 mitigation: increased egress capacity (NAT refresh) + aggressive prefix cache warming; error rate dropped to baseline by 03:05.

Maya: what I did while on-call: confirmed fallbacks behaved as expected, paused a non-essential canary that was amplifying short bursts, escalated to infra team for provider-side limits, left notes in the incident tracker.

Maya: current status: all systems green in metrics, no active pages. We still have two follow-ups for next shift (see actions below).

Devin: saw the spike on dashboards — good catch with the canary. FYI I left the temporary circuit-breaker rule in place (rule id: cb-usw-2100) to avoid another immediate spike while infra validated NAT capacity. Will remove after infra confirms provider config change.

Liam: added quick check to our runbook "egress-nat-exhaustion" — snippet I used:
```
# quick NAT exhaustion check
kubectl -n infra logs egress-proxy-0 --since=30m | grep -i "connect: cannot assign"
# if >1000 matches -> consider new IPs/NAT refresh
```
Linked that runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-nat-exhaustion (editable; leave notes)

Sophie: customer comms note — I patched the incident page with a brief summary and marked impacted customers for follow-up. Small cohort (3 customers) saw model-quality degradation; CS will reach out in morning with explanation + offer to re-run impacted requests if desired.

Anita: quick checklist for next shift (primary/secondary):
- Primary: verify cb-usw-2100 still blocking noisy ranges and remove only after infra signoff.
- Secondary: run the NAT exhaustion check (Liam snippet) and confirm provider quota increase ticket #INC-5821 is progressing.
- Both: validate model-variant routing metrics (percent traffic on v1-small) — should be <=5% now.

Maya: coverage note — incoming shift (today) we have primary: Devin, secondary: Liam. Night coverage gap at 06:00–07:30 UTC (Sophie is unavailable) — Devin + Liam agreed to short overlap check to cover the morning ramp.

Devin: can confirm I'll be primary through 10:00 UTC. I'll keep the circuit-breaker until infra OKs NAT change. Also will run a synthetic sweep across top 50 customers to ensure no lingering degradations.

Liam: will follow up on runbook edits and file a PR for clearer instruction around when to escalate to provider. Also will add a small dashboard panel: "egress new conn rate" + alert if connections/sec spikes > 1500 for 3m.

ops-bot: INCIDENT-LOG: page triggered at 2100000669 (egress-proxy 502 surge). Auto-routing initiated at 2100000720. Circuit-breaker applied cb-usw-2100. Event closed at 2100001500 (recovery).

deploy-bot: DEPLOY-NOTICE: rolled back canary service mylab/canary-v2 @ 2100001001 due to amplification of ephemeral connections. Rollback id: rb-2100-17. No further deploys in us-west until infra signoff.

Maya: next steps (actionable, assigned):
- Devin: keep cb-usw-2100 in place until infra confirms NAT quota increase (owner: Devin).
- Liam: add alert + PR for runbook (owner: Liam).
- Sophie: send customer follow-ups for impacted cohort (owner: Sophie).
- Anita: confirm postmortem template and schedule retrospective if postmortem indicates process gaps (owner: Anita).

Maya: any blockers for handoff? If none, I'm logging out. :wave:

Devin: no blockers here, will ping infra for the final signoff and update this thread.

Liam: nothing else. I'll pick up alerts and run the connection sweep at 03:30 local.

Sophie: all good. Leaving a short note for CS in Zendesk.

Anita: thanks — logging this into incident tracker INC-210000-PR-01 and assigning action items. No immediate customer SLA escalations.

Maya: thanks team. I'll check in for the 06:00 quick overlap. Handing over.
